 3 keys to victory for Montreal, Edmonton in the 113th Grey Cup 
 CALGARY — For the first time since 2015, the Edmonton Elks are Grey Cup champions.
 In a game that featured six lead changes, Edmonton held off the Montreal Alouettes in the fourth quarter to secure a 37-30 victory in the 113th Grey Cup on Sunday night at McMahon Stadium.
 The Elks came out firing, building a 21-point first-half performance in a back-and-forth opening 30 minutes before pulling away after the break. Quarterback Cody Fajardo ran for two touchdowns and threw for two more, finishing with 199 passing yards and 45 rushing yards against the team he helped lead to the Grey Cup in 2023.

 Running back Justin Rankin was crucial in the late stages, racking up 85 rushing yards on 13 carries, while Joshua Cephus reeled in two touchdowns.
 Montrell Washington got the Elks off to a roaring start, taking the opening kickoff 78 yards and bringing the crowd to life. Fajardo capped the quick drive with a one-yard plunge to get Edmonton on the board first.
 The Als answered on their first possession, with Davis Alexander completing four of his six passes for 66 yards, including a 26-yard catch-and-run by Tyson Philpot for the early equaliser.
 Edmonton followed with a two-and-out, but the result was made worse by an injury to All-CFL defensive back Tyrell Ford on Montreal's punt return. A roughing-the-passer penalty helped the Als move into scoring range, but with Ford sidelined, the Elks' secondary held firm in the red zone and forced a short field goal.
 Joe Robustelli jumpstarted Edmonton's next drive with a 29-yard catch, setting up a productive ground game as ShunDerrick Powell, Rankin and Fajardo helped move the Elks into scoring position. Fajardo finished the nine-play march with his second rushing touchdown of the half early in the second quarter.
 Montreal missed an opportunity on a fake sneak when Caleb Evans overthrew a streaking Philpot behind the defence, then let another chance slip away when Washington recovered his own muffed punt.
 Making his first start since Week 15, Kabion Ento made sure the Als capitalised on their next opportunity, picking off Fajardo and setting up Montreal with a short field. Evans finished the job with a goal-line sneak after another Edmonton penalty helped move the Als into scoring range.
 Edmonton reclaimed the lead before halftime, taking a 21-17 advantage on Fajardo's 11-yard touchdown pass to Cephus. The Elks pivot bounced back from his interception with a strong nine-play march, escaping the pocket for a chain-moving run on second-and-six and completing all four of his passes for 55 yards.
 The Alouettes offence opened the second half in rhythm, stringing together three consecutive gains of more than 15 yards before Alexander won a footrace to the pylon to put Montreal back in front.
 With just eight pass attempts in the first half, Fajardo and the Elks continued to lean on the ground game after the break. Powell set the tone, stiff-arming two defenders on a 19-yard run on his first touch of the half. But after crossing midfield, Edmonton shifted gears through the air, with Fajardo completing four straight passes, including a fade to Cephus at the back of the end zone for his second touchdown of the night.
 Malik Carney helped swing momentum back Edmonton's way, levelling Alexander as he disrupted a second-down attempt to Philpot and forced a punt. Alexander was shaken up but stayed in the game, and the Elks turned the stop into a field goal from Vincent Blanchard, taking a seven-point lead into the fourth quarter.
 The Als got back on the board early in the final frame, with Maltos Díaz converting from 25 yards to cut into the deficit. They quickly got the ball back when Don Callis punched it loose from Brendan O'Leary-Orange, but the Elks defence forced a two-and-out to keep Montreal off the scoreboard.
 Alexander continued to look downfield as the clock ticked away, searching for the big play that had defined the Alouettes offence throughout 2026. The Elks defence stood tall, keeping everything in front of them and denying Montreal a chance to get back into the game, while Edmonton's offence added two more field goals and leaned on its ground game to seal the victory.
 Alexander completed 21 of his 36 attempts for 226 yards and a touchdown in a second straight Grey Cup loss. Stevie Scott III added 133 rushing yards on 13 attempts, while Philpot had a game-high 80 receiving yards.
